description: Preregistered witness for the starting value of a delayed host automation queue after a parameter write between render blocks. This extends host-automation.json without changing its limits or predicates. It is a software state-ownership contract, not a CS-80 circuit law.

host_automation_state_boundary.truth: For a queue whose first point occurs after sample zero, the implicit sample -1 value is the latest parameter value at the boundary. An intervening native zero-frame parameter flush, UI setter or restored state supersedes an older automation endpoint. In the absence of an intervening write, retain the previous queue's full-precision normalized endpoint; do not introduce an extra float physical-to-normalized round trip at each block boundary.
witnesses: After prepare and one rendered block, issue a native VST3 zero-frame parameter flush with a new value, then render a queue whose first point is delayed. Compare every sample against an independent scalar schedule beginning at the flushed value, including samples before that first point.
Repeat after a completed automation curve, so the flushed value must replace an existing cached endpoint rather than only the initial default.

At processor-bridge level, repeat delayed-queue starts after setValueNotifyingHost and after the existing locked/synchronised APVTS state replacement path. The first sample and all subsequent samples must follow the latest stored parameter state.

Without an intervening write, carry a non-Float32-representable normalized endpoint into a delayed queue and require exact continuity from that double endpoint. Check the starting state directly, not only an audio threshold.

Exercise every enum-named key parameter, delayed first points at sample 1 and the final sample, and block sizes 7, 64 and 256. Preserve existing no-queue, Pure/Legacy, selected factory/memory and 16-voice assertions unchanged.

The native normalized-state reader must be observationally inert: identical zero-frame flush and delayed-queue renders, with and without connecting/synchronizing/disconnecting the native edit controller to read its current normalized state, must be byte-identical. Check both ordinary preceding blocks and completed preceding curves before using that reader as an oracle.
mutations: Restore stale cached automationCurrent as the implicit start even when the current parameter value changed between blocks; the state-boundary witness must fail.
Refresh the implicit start unconditionally from float parameter readback even when the last host endpoint has not been superseded; the exact endpoint-continuity witness must fail.
Delay boundary refresh until after the queue is attached; the delayed-first-point witness must fail.
Make the native state reader set a different parameter value after reading it; the exact native reader-neutrality witness must fail.
host_automation_state_boundary.registration_order: Commit this acceptance file before running the new witnesses or evaluating implementation changes. Record the unmodified failure, repaired result and mutation results. Existing host-automation.json limits remain authoritative for all original tests.

sources: Declared software inference: a successful parameter setter or state restore is authoritative at the next render boundary, while unchanged host-curve endpoints retain their already accepted full precision.
